It’s set to be one of the most groundbreaking moments in humanity’s six decades of space exploration: Today SpaceX was due to land a rocket on a floating platform after launching. But those looking forward to this pivotal moment will have to wait a little longer. 

SpaceX was aiming to complete a historic first: landing a Falcon 9 rocket at Cape Canaveral, Florida, following the launch of a Dragon spacecraft bound for the International Space Station (ISS). This ambitious attempt – to land the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket on solid ground after taking the Dragon capsule to space – was scheduled to take place today, a plan that has now hit a snarl. 

The launch, which had initially been slated for earlier this week, was postponed due to an issue with one of the rocket's engines. That problem persists, and as a result, the ambitious landing attempt is rescheduled for 11.18am GMT on Tuesday, January 6th.

The landing barge, known as the Of Course I Still Love You, waited off the coast of Cape Canaveral, prepared to welcome the Falcon 9 back from the heavens. SpaceX, led by visionary CEO Elon Musk, has repeatedly emphasized the importance and challenge of reusability in space travel, aiming to revolutionize the industry with fully reusable rockets that could drastically cut down the cost of space travel.

Elon Musk has openly stated the chances of a successful landing on solid ground as 50%, acknowledging the high-risk nature of such experimental attempts.

**For Immediate Release**

**Sister of Suspect in Malala Yousufzai Attack Publicly Apologizes**

**Rawalpindi, Pakistan –** In an unexpected turn of events, the sister of a man suspected in the shooting of Pakistani teenage education activist Malala Yousufzai has publicly apologized to the victim. Rehana Haleem, sister of the 23-year-old student Atta Ullah Khan, said her brother's actions have brought irreparable shame to their family.

"He has brought shame on our family," stated Rehana Haleem in an emotional press conference held today in Rawalpindi. "I don't consider Atta Ullah my brother anymore," she added, breaking her silence on the matter.

Atta Ullah Khan is being sought by authorities in connection with the attack on Malala, who was shot in the head by gunmen last Tuesday while returning home from school in her hometown of Mingora. Malala, a vocal advocate for girls' education in the Swat Valley, has been hospitalized and is recovering after surgery in the United Kingdom.

Rehana Haleem reached out to the public and Malala herself through the media, extending an apology on behalf of her estranged brother.

"Please convey a message to Malala, that I apologize for what my brother did to her," she said, her voice shaking with emotion.

Her apology comes as law enforcement officials continue their efforts to locate Atta Ullah Khan, who is believed to have ties to Taliban-linked militants. The suspect remains at large, prompting concerns among authorities and human rights organizations.

**Russia Accused of Sending Tanks into Ukraine Amid Peace Process Tensions**

Russia was accused of sending tanks into Ukraine for the first time yesterday while the West’s attention was diverted by the chaos in Iraq. The development threatens to destroy the tentative peace process just when the US and EU had hoped Vladimir Putin had agreed to ease tensions in the region.

Interior Minister Arseny Avakov of Ukraine announced tanks had entered the country through a checkpoint controlled by pro-Russian separatists in the Luhansk region. This marks a significant escalation in the conflict, which has seen Ukraine's Eastern provinces gripped by unrest for months.

Russia has vehemently denied these claims, reaffirming that it is not aiding the separatists who have taken control of several towns and cities in mainly Russian-speaking east Ukraine. President Vladimir Putin has previously called for dialogue and pledged to tighten controls at borders to help ease the situation.

Ukrainian authorities claim the tanks crossing into Ukrainian territory are evidence of Russian military involvement, a claim that, if proven, could lead to further economic and diplomatic sanctions against Russia by the West.

The situation adds a new layer of complexity to the already precarious peace process. Just days ago, there were signs of hope with statements from all parties suggesting a willingness to negotiate and implement a ceasefire. However, the reported incursion of Russian tanks will likely provoke a strong reaction from Kiev and its Western allies.

**Genealogist Tries to Fill Out Details of Doomed Civil War Submarine Crew**

One investigative tip can lead to another -- and another. Linda Abrams, a genealogy gumshoe, went to Texas to match handwriting samples. She spent a couple weeks in Kentucky following a tip, only to find it was just hearsay. Yet, her relentless quest has shed light on the mysterious lives of the eight men who crewed the Hunley, one of the most intriguing and tragic tales from the Civil War.

The Hunley, the first successful combat submarine in history, sank a Union sloop off the coast of South Carolina in February 1864, a feat that sent shockwaves through the Union Navy. However, in a stunning twist of fate, the sub itself was lost shortly thereafter, claiming the lives of its entire crew. For over a century and a half, the identities and backgrounds of these sailors remained largely a mystery.

Abrams' journey began in earnest after a chance encounter with a historian who shared the names of the crewmen, many of whom were previously undocumented. Over the past few years, she has used genealogical databases, court records, and old letters to piece together the puzzle of each man's life.

DNA has proven elusive for all but one of the sailors, making traditional identification through genetic markers an arduous task. This has pushed Abrams and her team to rely on more traditional genealogical methods, an undertaking she describes as "a breadcrumb trail." The process is painstaking, and she has been faced with dead ends and false leads.

One of the more intriguing questions that has lingered over the years pertains to the life of the Hunley’s captain, Lt. George E. Dixon.

Michael Jackson's Life and Legacy: Katherine Jackson Testifies on Son's Early Days

Michael Jackson's life began on August 29, 1958, as the seventh child in a family crowded into a tiny home in Gary, Indiana. His mother, Katherine Jackson, remembers "a sweet little child" who showed unusual empathy for others and who was always interested in music. In an emotional testimony earlier this week, Katherine shared stories of her son's early days as the family continues to navigate through the ongoing trial centered around the King of Pop's estate.

Thursday marked what would have been Michael Jackson's 55th birthday, providing an opportunity for reflection on the impact of the man who transformed the music industry and captivated audiences worldwide.

In her moving testimony, Katherine detailed Michael's initial foray into public performance, recalling his heartwarming rendition of "Climb Every Mountain" during a kindergarten program. "He sang it with such clarity and didn't miss—not flat or anything," she said, her eyes filled with the pride of a mother who witnessed her son's talent blossom from an early age.

The Jackson family lived in near-poverty conditions, yet music was a constant presence, nurturing young Michael's passion and skill.

Police in Rotherham have come under fire for holding a self-congratulatory awards ceremony just two weeks after a damning report accused the force of letting down sexually abused children. A ceremony in the town last week praised officers for going 'above and beyond the call of duty,' according to statements made by police bosses during the event held at Rotherham United's New York Stadium.

The South Yorkshire Police awards gala, an occasion meant to honor the brave efforts and commitment of officers, took place against a backdrop of intense scrutiny. Just two weeks prior, a report by Her Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary (HMIC) found significant failings within the force, particularly in its response to child sexual exploitation in the Rotherham area. The report highlighted how officers had neglected their duty to protect vulnerable children who had been subjected to horrific abuse over many years.

The awards event, advertised on Facebook with images of smiling officers receiving accolades, was met with a wave of criticism from local communities and officials alike. Shaun Wright, the Police and Crime Commissioner for South Yorkshire, expressed concerns over the way the ceremony was publicised. He described it as "misguided" and warned that it risked overshadowing the serious issues raised in the report. Wright, who formerly served as Rotherham's chief executive, has faced calls to resign following the report's publication.

**CNN Anchor Stirs Controversy with Vulgar Twitter Tirade Against Fox News**

CNN anchor Bill Weir is causing a stir over his recent vulgar Twitter tirade against rival network Fox News. Bill Weir, who joined CNN from ABC News last fall, took to social media in response to a Fox Nation story with the headline, 'Climate Doesn’t Cooperate With Al Gore’s Group’s Visit to Denver EPA Hearings.' 

In his tweet, Weir lashed out, using explicit language to critique the Fox News coverage. The tweet quickly gained attention, sparking debates on social media about the role of journalists and respect in public discourse. 

Weir's response was particularly pointed, directing his ire at both the Fox headline and the perceived implications regarding climate change, a subject associated with former Vice President Al Gore. 

Not long after posting, Weir issued a public apology, acknowledging that his comments were inappropriate and crossed the line. "I let my frustration get the better of me and used language that I regret," he wrote, signaling a retreat from his combative stance.

**Centro. Alba. Zombie Burger. The dining scene in Des Moines is pretty hot these days. So why did nearly a thousand Iowans pay $100-a-pop last Saturday night to chew wilted salads and poke at dried-out chicken?** 

The answer is political pageantry, as Democrats from across Iowa gathered for their annual Jefferson-Jackson Dinner, an event steeped in tradition that has served as a cornerstone of the state's pivotal role in national politics.

Held at the Iowa Events Center, the dinner's attendees represented more than just a feast for the ears—this was a culinary offering that bore the weight of political aspiration and the promise of the Hawkeye State's influence in the 2020 presidential race. With speeches from the state's senior senator, Chuck Grassley, and a variety of Democratic hopefuls, the dinner served as much as a platform for political aspiration as it did a stage for speeches that could sway the future of American leadership.

Attendees were treated to an evening that was far removed from the gourmet delights Des Moines is famous for. Instead, they indulged in a more rustic and perhaps fittingly humble affair—a meal that echoed the state's agricultural roots rather than its burgeoning foodie culture.

"Even as we enjoy the rich culinary tapestry Des Moines now offers, there is something uniquely appropriate about gathering in this manner, over a modest dinner, to address the future of our nation," commented one attendee, Susan Jennings, a long-time Democrat and voter from the Des Moines area.

The evening was marked by a series of speeches that underlined the candidates' resolve, vision, and the importance they place on Iowa's early primaries.

**France's Charles de Gaulle Aircraft Carrier Begins Anti-ISIS Operations in Iraq**

Paris, France — France's Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier has started military operations against the Islamic State (ISIS) in Iraq, a French army source disclosed today. The first Rafale fighter jet took off this morning from the French flagship as it sailed about 120 miles off the Iraqi coast, marking a significant escalation in France's involvement in the ongoing battle against the militant group.

Naval sources have indicated that the deployment will "participate in missions for several weeks," highlighting France's commitment to supporting Iraqi forces in their fight against ISIS. The French carrier's presence and the subsequent airstrike missions signify an increased operational tempo in the anti-ISIS coalition's efforts to eradicate the group's presence in the region.

According to monitors, U.S.-led airstrikes have already resulted in the deaths of over 1,600 people, a vast majority of whom are ISIS terrorists. However, the reports also reveal a troubling toll on civilians, with 62 non-combatants killed in the process. This deployment by France is part of an ongoing effort to strengthen the coalition's offensive against ISIS, aiming not only to degrade the group's capabilities but also to protect vulnerable civilian populations.

This move by France comes amid international criticism over the civilian casualties and the overall effectiveness of the coalition's operations.

**Anxious Relatives of MH370 Passengers Await News Amidst Vigils and Online Tributes**

New Zealanders Danica and Paul Weeks are no strangers to disaster. The couple's eldest son, Lincoln, was born in the midst of an earthquake in Christchurch in 2010. Just over three years later, in December 2013, they faced another harrowing ordeal when Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 (MH370) disappeared en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing, carrying their youngest son, Dylan, among its 239 passengers and crew.

As the search for MH370 entered its seventh year with hopes of finding the missing aircraft and any potential survivors fading, the Weeks, along with numerous other relatives of passengers on board, continue to hold onto hope and fear for their loved ones.

Among those on the ill-fated flight was Ju Kun, a martial arts star known for his skills in the Chinese kicking form of "sandao." His participation in a reality TV show before boarding the flight made him a familiar face to many, sparking an outpouring of tributes and support online. Social media platforms have been inundated with Ju Kun's videos and memories shared by fans and fellow martial artists, all mourning the loss and celebrating his life and talents.

"Each day without closure is another day of uncertainty and sorrow," said Angela Zhang, Ju Kun's sister. "But the online tributes have been a comfort in our time of grief; they remind us that he lived a life worth celebrating and that he touched many hearts."
